findings.observation: The appendix says that the ASR paper's 'unspecified exact aggregate audio duration' prevents a precise reconstruction of real-time factor. The archived original paper explicitly gives a total clean-audio duration of 328 seconds in its Table 3 heading.

locations: Page 7, whisperx-base FP16 row, file line 230
original_evidence.quote: Table 3: Energy use and inference time for fp16 precision, clean audio (duration: 328 seconds)
original_evidence.supporting_detail: The FP16 base row repeats 78.0 seconds and 155 J in Tables 3 and 4. The measurement setup says the CPU+GPU idle baseline is subtracted. A known aggregate duration supports aggregate processing-time/audio-duration arithmetic; it does not turn this into continuous-stream latency, peak/sustained throughput or whole-device wall energy.

findings.impact: This creates a false missing-data limitation in the current deliverable. It does not invalidate Section 6's base-versus-medium precision comparison or justify replacing the report's sustained-operation qualification. The accurate boundary is between aggregate clean-clip results and a qualified continuous service; lack of whole-box energy measurement is separate from whether duration was reported.
findings.required_change: Correct only the false duration claim. State that Table 3 reports 328 seconds of clean audio, while retaining the limits on continuous-service performance and whole-device wall energy. No additional experiment or source search is needed.
findings.suggested_replacement: Table 3 reports 328 seconds of clean audio, which supports aggregate real-time-factor arithmetic from its processing times. These clip-based totals do not establish sustained continuous-stream latency or whole-device wall energy.
findings.scope_note: The erroneous sentence is unchanged in the supplied editorial diff. It was discovered directly while checking the revised medium-INT8 interpretation against the same original paper; it is not attributed to this revision.

Source checks were deliberately directed at edited claims, retained conditions and directly affected interpretations. Unchanged claims outside those checks were not independently revalidated.
